questions.question: Is the limit per-key or per-IP?
questions.best_guess: Per-key — the gateway auth middleware resolves keys before routing (gateway/auth.py:41).

questions.question: What happens to rejected requests?
questions.best_guess: 429 with Retry-After, matching the incident log's remediation note (INC-113).

questions.question: Does the health endpoint bypass the limiter?
questions.best_guess: Yes — probes already bypass auth (gateway/routes.py:12), so the limiter should sit behind that branch.

rewritten_request: Add per-API-key rate limiting to the gateway behind the existing auth middleware, returning 429 with Retry-After, exempting the unauthenticated health probe path, sized against the INC-113 traffic profile.

questions.question: Where did the name RetryQueue come from?
questions.best_guess: A sibling service's vocabulary — the brief's author last worked in ingestd, which has one.

questions.question: Is the real goal retries for archival uploads, regardless of mechanism?
questions.best_guess: Yes — the outcome, not the helper, is load-bearing.

questions.question: Should the inline backoff be extracted first?
questions.best_guess: No — extend the existing inline pattern (exporter.py:88) rather than introducing a new abstraction mid-task.

rewritten_request: Make archival uploads in the exporter retry with the same inline exponential backoff the module already uses at exporter.py:88; there is no RetryQueue helper in this codebase and none should be invented for this change.

questions.question: Are the three importers reading private fields on purpose?
questions.best_guess: No — convenience imports that predate the parser's public accessor (parser.py:23).

questions.question: Does billing round-trip the parsed dates?
questions.best_guess: Yes — billing/serialize.py:57 re-serializes with the old format string.

questions.question: Is a compatibility shim acceptable?
questions.best_guess: Yes for one release — audit's importer is frozen until Q4 per its module docstring.

rewritten_request: Change the config parser's date handling AND update the three private-internal importers (billing/serialize.py, audit/ingest.py, reports/export.py) in the same change, or land a one-release compatibility shim; the change is not local to the parser.

questions.question: Does the named logging facade exist anywhere reachable?
questions.best_guess: No — repo-wide search is empty; the brief likely means the facade proposed in the design doc that never landed.

questions.question: Should the facade be built before any migration?
questions.best_guess: Yes — one agent builds it first, or the fan-out has no target.

questions.question: Do the four modules even share a logging pattern today?
questions.best_guess: Only two do — the other two log via the metrics wrapper (metrics/log.py:19).

rewritten_request: Do not dispatch four migrations against a facade that does not exist. First land the logging facade from the unmerged design doc as its own bounded change; then re-scope the fan-out to the two modules that actually use direct logging.

questions.question: Which timeout actually killed the nightly job?
questions.best_guess: The scheduler watchdog — the nightly failure log shows job-level kills at exactly 3600s, not per-request errors.

questions.question: Is raising the watchdog safe for other jobs?
questions.best_guess: It is per-job configurable (scheduler/config.py:31), so no global change is needed.

questions.question: Should the HTTP deadline change too?
questions.best_guess: No — no per-request timeout appears in the failure log.

rewritten_request: Raise the scheduler's job-level watchdog for the nightly export job only (per-job setting at scheduler/config.py:31); leave the HTTP client's per-request deadline untouched — the failure log implicates the watchdog, not the client.

questions.question: Is the refund path idempotent under retry?
questions.best_guess: No — the handler posts the ledger entry before the dedupe check (refund.py:74), which is what INC-207 documents.

questions.question: Why does the regression test pass anyway?
questions.best_guess: It stubs the ledger client, so double-posts never surface (test_refund.py:19).

questions.question: Is the brief's 'rare double-refund' premise right?
questions.best_guess: Wrong — INC-207 shows it is every retry after a gateway timeout, not rare.

questions.question: What would disconfirm the dedupe hypothesis?
questions.best_guess: A double-post with distinct idempotency keys in the ledger export; none found in the sampled week.

rewritten_request: Fix the refund handler's ordering so the dedupe check precedes the ledger post (refund.py:74), un-stub the ledger client in the regression test, and treat INC-207's every-retry failure profile — not 'rare double-refunds' — as the acceptance condition.

questions.question: Why was the flag left true?
questions.best_guess: The cache-bypass experiment ended in June but its cleanup ticket is still open (TCK-981).

questions.question: Does anything depend on the bypass being on?
questions.best_guess: Unknown for the warm-up job — its reads are still uninspected; carried as an open coupling question.

questions.question: Is the flag the whole latency story?
questions.best_guess: Mostly — the graph inflects at the flag's deploy date, but the cache layer's TTL remains unexamined.

rewritten_request: Flip the stale cache-bypass flag at config.py:88 to false as the first change, gated on confirming the warm-up job does not depend on the bypass; then re-measure before touching cache TTLs.
